brief: Why I quit my 9-to-5 — and what I'd do differently if I started over.

slots.title: SNAP POINT
slots.body: I ignored burnout for six months until a Tuesday panic attack in a parking lot rewrote my priorities overnight.

slots.title: NO PLAN
slots.body: I handed in my notice with no savings runway and no client pipeline, trading one stress for a deeper, quieter dread.

slots.title: SKILL FIRST
slots.body: If I started over, I would monetize one proven skill before quitting, letting the side income validate the leap.

slots.title: SAVE FIRST
slots.body: Three months of expenses is the minimum; six buys you the calm to say no to bad clients and worse projects.

slots.title: TALK EARLY
slots.body: I wish I had told trusted peers about my exit three months sooner; opportunities arrive faster when people know you're leaving.

slots.title: WORTH IT
slots.body: The first year was harder than the job, yet reclaiming my mornings, mind, and margin made every risk feel inevitable.

slots.headline: GO
slots.body: Quit the dream of quitting blindly; build the runway first, then leap with your eyes wide open.
